recognize_zh: 中央白血球細胞質邊緣有數顆粗大的黑褐色瘧色素（hemozoin）顆粒；背景紅血球大量感染細小環狀體、多重感染與 appliqué 型，並有少數深染長形寄生蟲體，符合重度惡性瘧（P. falciparum）伴隨吞噬瘧色素的白血球。
features: Central leukocyte with a band-like to minimally segmented nucleus and pink granular cytoplasm containing a cluster of coarse black-brown hemozoin granules
Numerous red cells with small delicate ring forms, many multiply infected, with appliqué forms
Scattered compact dark-staining elongated parasite forms, some pigmented, suggestive of maturing stages or gametocytes
Infected red cells normal in size without Schüffner stippling
Mild red cell overlap in thick areas limits assessment of some forms
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows high-grade parasitemia with numerous small ring forms, frequent multiply infected red cells and appliqué forms in normal-sized erythrocytes. Scattered compact, darkly staining elongated parasites, some containing pigment, are also present. A central neutrophil contains coarse black-brown intracytoplasmic granules consistent with phagocytosed malarial pigment (hemozoin). Findings are consistent with severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria with pigment-laden neutrophils.

ddx.vs: Babesia rings are pleomorphic with tetrads and produce no hemozoin, so pigment in leukocytes excludes it.
P. malariae shows band-form trophozoites and rosette schizonts with low parasitemia, not heavy multiple ring infection.

ddx.dx: Coarse toxic granulation or Alder-Reilly granules
ddx.vs: Toxic and Alder-Reilly granules are purple-violet and uniformly distributed rather than refractile black-brown clumps.
Precipitate lies on top of cells and in the background, whereas hemozoin is confined within cytoplasm in the same focal plane.
